assertions.source: The sigma^-1 letters the 'd == 0' rule dropped. Non-zero is the correction; the value is the size of it on 2H.

description: Census of the atom word's letters by whether they lie in the image of rho : B_n -> H_n(q). Confirms the two counts the atom_braid_word_3A docstring rests its no-single-link argument on (averaged letters = 2A+1; 2^(2A+1) = 32 branch closures for 2H), and corrects its 'only d == 0 letters are braid generators' parenthetical: under the module's own sigma^-1 = sigma - h, the d == -h letters are braid generators too.

correction.was: Only the `d == 0` letters are braid generators.
correction.measured_on_2H: 23 letters: 11 sigma, 7 sigma^-1, 5 averaged. So 18 are braid generators, not 11.
correction.why_it_matters: under a 'd == 0' rule the figure-eight (s1 s2^-1)^2 -- the muon carrier, a genuine hyperbolic LINK the mass law reads Vol from -- would classify as 'not a braid word'. The no-single-link conclusion belongs to the atom object and must not leak onto the knot-dictionary carriers.
correction.what_is_CONFIRMED_not_corrected: the substance. The atom object IS outside im(rho), the averaged count IS 2A+1, and 2^5 = 32 DOES match the SnapPy sweep. Only the parenthetical was wrong.
